description: Welcome to Laiba’s Ghost Probes , a global team registered for the Universal Event at the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge! Led by Laiba Mubasher from the Institute of Space Science, University of the Punjab, we are tackling the Abandoned But Not Forgotten challenge. Using official records from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), we tell the stories of NASA’s silent pioneers—from Voyager 1 and Pioneer 10 to Spirit, Opportunity, and Ingenuity.
summary: Abandoned But Not Forgotten explores the legacy of NASA’s historic spacecraft, rovers, and landers left across the Moon, Mars, and deep interstellar space since the 1960s. Using verified mission data from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), our project profiles iconic hardware—including Voyager 1, Pioneer 10, Spirit, Opportunity, and Ingenuity—detailing their launch dates, scientific breakthroughs, and the exact technical reasons they eventually went silent or were left behind. Rather than viewing these retired machines as lost, our project demonstrates how their archived measurements continue to fuel new scientific discoveries, guide the engineering of future planetary missions, and inspire the next generation of global space explorers.
details:
What Our Project Does
Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an educational storytelling and data showcase highlighting NASA’s historic hardware left across the Moon, Mars, and deep space since the 1960s. Instead of viewing silent probes and retired rovers as lost machines, our project preserves their operational timelines, scientific milestones, and final fates so students and space enthusiasts worldwide can learn from their journeys.

Key Missions Featured
Using official records from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) Master Catalog, we profile major off-world explorers—including Voyager 1, Voyager 2, Pioneer 10, Pioneer 11, Spirit, Opportunity, Ingenuity, Apollo landers, Surveyor, Viking, Sojourner, Phoenix, InSight, Lunar Roving Vehicles, Mars Pathfinder, Mars Polar Lander, and Mars Climate Orbiter. For our core case studies, we break down each mission's launch date, scientific purpose, and exact technical reason it was left behind:

  • Voyager 1 (Launched 1977): Completed a grand tour of Jupiter and Saturn before entering interstellar space in 2012, now coasting beyond servicing range as its nuclear power source weakens.
  • Pioneer 10 (Launched 1972): The first probe to cross the asteroid belt and fly by Jupiter, sending its final faint signal in January 2003 as its radioisotope power decayed.
  • Spirit Rover (Launched 2003): Searched Gusev Crater for evidence of past water until soft sand prevented its solar panels from tilting toward the winter Sun in 2010.
  • Opportunity Rover (Launched 2003): Outlived its planned mission by 14 years while uncovering mineral evidence of ancient Martian water before a global dust storm blocked its solar panels in 2018.
  • Ingenuity Helicopter (Launched 2020): Completed 72 powered flights on Mars—far beyond its planned 5—before rough-landing blade damage ended its mission in January 2024.
Why It Matters
Every silent spacecraft leaves behind three lasting contributions: archived measurements in NASA’s databases ready for new discoveries, engineering lessons that guide future rovers and aircraft, and inspiration for the next generation of explorers.
